title: He cast out demons.
paragraphs: He cast out demons.
And still… was shut out of heaven.
Let that sink in.

Not a pagan.
Not an atheist.
Not someone who hated Jesus.

This man used the name of Christ.
Moved in power.
Stood in moments that looked like revival.
And yet—Jesus says something that should shake every soul awake:

“Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and do many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness.’” — Matthew 7:22–23
Many.

Not a few.
Not a rare case.
Many.

This is not just a warning.
This is a mirror.

Because it exposes a terrifying truth:
You can do things for Jesus… and still not belong to Jesus.

You can speak His name publicly…
But never surrender to Him privately.

You can rebuke darkness…
While secretly entertaining sin.

You can build a platform…
And still have no prayer life.

You can impress people…
And still be unknown in heaven.
Pause.
This is where the tension tightens.

Because in our generation, we celebrate gifts more than godliness.
We amplify charisma over character.
We chase manifestations… but neglect intimacy.
But Jesus doesn’t deny their works.
He doesn’t say, “That didn’t happen.”
He says, “I never knew you.”

That word—knew—is not information.
It is relationship.

Covenant.
Communion.
Belonging.

These men had activity… but not intimacy.
Power… but not purity.
Ministry… but not mastery under Christ.
And then comes the word that burns:
Lawlessness.

Not weakness that runs back to God.
Not a believer fighting sin and crying out for mercy.

Lawlessness is a life that refuses the rule of Christ
while still trying to use His name.
It is rebellion… wearing church clothes.
And this is where it gets personal.
Because this is not just about “them.”
This is about us.

Do you love Jesus…
Or just what He can do through you?

Do you pursue His presence…
Or just His power?

Do you obey Him when no one sees…
Or only when it benefits your image?
Because the scariest deception is not being far from God…

It is thinking you are close—
when you are not.

Even Judas walked with Jesus.
He heard His voice.
Saw His miracles.
Handled holy things.
And still betrayed Him.

Some scholars interpret Matthew 7 as a warning against false disciples whose outward works were never rooted in true repentance and regeneration. Not everyone who ministers is truly surrendered. Not everyone who speaks His name is transformed by His grace.
That should not make you paranoid.
But it should make you honest.
Here is the mercy hidden inside this warning:

Jesus tells us this now—
so we don’t hear it later.

This is not just judgment.
This is invitation.
He is not trying to push you away.
He is calling you closer.

Away from performance.
Away from pretending.
Away from religious masks.
Into real relationship.
Into surrender.
Into truth.
Because the Gospel is not about becoming impressive.
It is about becoming new.

You don’t earn your way into being known by Christ.
You don’t perform your way into heaven.
You repent.
You believe.
You surrender.

The same Jesus who warns in Matthew 7
is the same Jesus who went to the cross for sinners.

For hypocrites.
For the double-hearted.
For those who got it wrong.

He lived the perfect life you couldn’t live.
He died the death your sins deserved.
He rose again—not just to display power,
but to offer you a new heart.
Not just ministry.
Identity.
Not just gifts.
Grace.
So stop trying to impress Him.
He already sees everything.

What He wants…
is you.

Your real heart.
Your hidden places.
Your private life.
Come clean.

Repent of the sin you’ve been excusing.
Let go of the image you’ve been protecting.
Lay down the version of Christianity that costs you nothing.
And come to Jesus.
Fully.
Honestly.
Now.

Because on that final day,
the greatest miracle will not be what you did in His name—
It will be hearing Him say:
“I know you.”
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
